week.weeklyOverview: This week toddlers become gentle pet helpers. They explore stuffed pets, practice simple caregiving (wash, brush, feed, rest), and try a toddler-friendly vet clinic with only a few clear props. The week stays play-based and short-turn focused—no worksheets, no tiny medical pieces, and no pressure for perfect crafts. Teachers should expect parallel play, brief attention bursts, and lots of repetition with the same pets and care words.
week.objectives:
Social-emotional: Practice gentle touch, turn-taking, and caregiving roles with peers and pets.
Language: Hear and try pet-care words such as gentle, wash, brush, listen, bandage, and rest.
Cognitive: Follow simple care sequences and notice pet body parts in pictures and play.
Fine motor: Scoop, brush, stamp, and sticker with large toddler tools.
Gross motor: Crawl, march, carry, and freeze during pet movement games.
Sensory: Explore wet/dry wash play and soft/bumpy pet textures with safe materials.
Creative: Make process paw-print charts and open-ended pet collars/collages.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Everyday: stuffed/plastic pets, baskets, bowls, spoons, cloths, blankets, blocks, boxes, painter’s tape, smocks, towels
Art: washable paint, paper, large stickers, stampers, glue sticks, pre-cut shapes, yarn scraps
Sensory: shallow tub, mild soap, shredded paper or kinetic sand (optional), scoops
Dramatic play: toy stethoscope, large fabric bandages, helper badges, short ribbon leashes, waiting cushions
Literacy: Biscuit Visits the Doctor; Harry the Dirty Dog; Doctor Maisy; optional Sally Goes to the Vet
Optional printables: clinic zone signs; pet care choice cards
week.teacherPreparation:
Before Monday: sanitize pets/tools; remove tiny vet-kit pieces; pre-cut collar strips and collage shapes.
Set up reusable clinic zones (Waiting / Exam / Resting) that can stay all week.
Prep one art tray and one sensory tub plan; alternate wet days to manage cleanup.
Choose 2–3 books and place them in the reading basket.
Print clinic signs if using; laminate for reuse.
prepChecklist: Pre-cut collar strips and large collage shapes
week.observationFocus:
Gentle vs rough touch with support
Care vocabulary attempts
Turn-taking at popular centers
Persistence in pretend sequences
Sensory preferences during wash/texture play
Gross-motor listening (start/stop)
week.familyConnection: Invite families to notice a pet or animal helper on the way home, or cuddle a stuffed animal and practice one gentle care word together (wash, brush, rest). Optional: send a photo of a family pet if they wish—no required homework.
week.adaptations: Offer watching-first entry, fewer props, dry-bath alternatives, shorter paths, and picture sequence supports. Never force holding pets.

activities.title: Meet the Pets
activities.objective: Warmly introduce stuffed and toy pets so toddlers can look, touch, name, and choose a favorite animal companion for the week.
activities.description: Toddlers explore a small collection of soft pets on a low table or rug. They may hold, hug, point, or carry a pet while the teacher models gentle touch and simple pet words.
activities.materials:
4–6 large stuffed or soft plastic pets (dog, cat, bunny, bird)
Low table or floor mat
Basket for pets
Optional: pet photo cards (large)
activities.preparation:
Sanitize pets and basket
Place only 4–6 pets out (avoid clutter)
Set photo cards nearby if using
activities.setup: Arrange pets in an open basket on a rug with space for 2–3 toddlers to sit or kneel. Keep walkways clear.
activities.steps:
1. Sit at toddler level and greet one pet by name.
2. Invite each child to choose a pet to hold or look at.
3. Model gentle petting with an open palm.
4. Offer simple words: soft, dog, cat, gentle.
5. Allow free exploration; rotate pets if needed.
6. End by helping pets “rest” in the basket.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Who is this pet?
Can you give a gentle pet?
Is your pet soft?
Where should the dog rest?
You are being so careful.
activities.observationOpportunities: Notice approaching/avoiding, naming attempts, gentle vs rough touch, and whether children share space with peers.
activities.safetyNotes: Use pets too large to choke on. Remove loose eyes/buttons. Sanitize after mouthing. Supervise closely.
activities.cleanupTips: Return pets to the basket. Spot-clean any mouthed toys before the next group.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Use a quiet corner rug if the room is busy.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Bring a small pet basket outdoors on a blanket for shade play.
teacherTips: Start with fewer pets for younger toddlers.
If a child only watches, narrate what peers are doing without pressure.

substitutions.use: Clean socks with faces drawn on + soft fabric “blankets”

activities.adaptations: Offer hand-under-hand support for gentle touch. Allow watching first. Provide a second identical pet if sharing is hard.
activities.extensions: Invite toddlers to “feed” a pet with pretend bowls after choosing.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers can help “introduce” pets to younger friends with one word labels.
observationPrompts: Did the child choose a pet independently?
Did they attempt a pet name or animal sound?
Was touch gentle with support?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Realistic daycare rug setup with a basket of large stuffed pets and toddler-sized space. Hands/props focus preferred. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Veterinarian Dramatic Play Center
activities.objective: Practice caregiving pretend play in a simple toddler vet clinic using a few clear props and short role turns.
activities.description: Toddlers pretend to be pet helpers: bring a stuffed pet to the “exam table,” listen with a toy stethoscope, wrap a large bandage, and rest the pet in a waiting spot.
activities.materials:
Low table as exam table (paper cover optional)
2–3 stuffed pets
1–2 toy stethoscopes
Large soft bandage strips (fabric)
Waiting chairs or cushions
Optional: play doctor kit with SMALL pieces removed
activities.preparation:
Remove tiny kit pieces (syringes with needles, pills, etc.)
Tape paper on exam table if desired
Stage waiting cushions + 2 pets ready
activities.setup: Create three clear zones: Waiting cushions, Exam table, Resting basket. Keep props limited so the story stays simple.
activities.steps:
1. Show the three zones with short labels or picture signs.
2. Model: pet waits → helper listens → gentle bandage → rest.
3. Invite 1–2 toddlers at a time to the exam table.
4. Narrate caregiving language while children lead.
5. Rotate roles: helper and pet owner.
6. Close clinic by resting pets together.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Is your pet waiting?
Can you listen to the heartbeat?
Does the paw need a bandage?
All better?
Who is the helper now?
Let’s put the pet in the resting basket.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe role-taking, turn-taking, caregiving language, and persistence with multi-step pretend sequences.
activities.safetyNotes: No small parts. Bandages large only. Keep stethoscope cords short/supervised. No real medicines.
activities.cleanupTips: Sort props into Waiting / Exam / Resting bins. Wipe exam table.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Clinic fits a dramatic-play corner all week.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Move exam table under shade with the same three zones.
teacherTips: Less is best: 2 tools max at first.
Join as a co-player briefly, then step back.

substitutions.use: Paper cup “listener” on a short yarn loop (supervised)

activities.adaptations: Offer a one-step job (“put pet on table”). Allow parallel play. Picture sequence cards for the three steps.
activities.extensions: Add a “check-in” clipboard with a large pet photo to point to (no writing required).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Preschool visitors can be receptionists; toddlers stay on hands-on pet care.
observationPrompts: Did the child attempt more than one clinic step?
Did they use any care words?
How did they handle waiting?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Realistic toddler vet dramatic-play setup: low exam table, stuffed dog, toy stethoscope, large bandage, waiting cushions. No cartoon look. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Pet Movement Parade
activities.objective: Move like familiar pets to build body awareness, listening, and joyful gross-motor play.
activities.description: Toddlers parade around a clear path pretending to be dogs, cats, bunnies, or birds using simple movements: crawl, tip-toe, hop, or flap.
activities.materials:
Open floor path or outdoor sidewalk loop
Optional animal picture cards
Music player (optional, soft volume)
activities.preparation:
Clear trip hazards
Choose 3 movements max
Place start/finish markers (tape or cones)
activities.setup: Mark a simple oval path. Hold up one animal card at a time.
activities.steps:
1. Show the dog card and crawl like a puppy.
2. Invite toddlers to follow the path.
3. Switch to cat tip-toe, then bunny hop.
4. Pause for resting pets.
5. End with a gentle pet parade back to the rug.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Can you crawl like a puppy?
Tip-toe, quiet cats!
Hop, hop, bunny!
Freeze — resting pets.
Where is your tail?
activities.observationOpportunities: Watch balance, imitation, stopping/starting on cue, and enjoyment of group movement.
activities.safetyNotes: Space children out. No running indoors. Soft landings for hops. Outdoor surfaces dry/clear.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Use hallway laps with walking feet only.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Use a playground loop; add “bird wings” arm flaps.
teacherTips: Offer a wagon push option for children who prefer wheeled movement.

substitutions.use: Hold up stuffed pets as movement cues

activities.adaptations: Offer hand-holding for balance. Allow stroller/walker users to shake a bell as the parade sound.
activities.extensions: Let a child choose the next animal movement.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants can watch and bounce on a caregiver’s lap; older toddlers lead the line.
observationPrompts: Did the child imitate at least one animal move?
Could they stop on “freeze”?

activities.title: Feed the Pets
activities.objective: Practice caregiving routines by pretending to prepare and offer food/water to stuffed pets.
activities.description: Toddlers scoop dry oats or crumpled paper “kibble” into bowls and offer pretend water cups to their pets, then wipe mouths with cloths.
activities.materials:
Stuffed pets
Small bowls
Spoons/scoops
Dry oats OR crumpled brown paper “kibble”
Cups for pretend water
Cloths for wiping
activities.preparation:
Portion filler into a shallow bin
Set bowls on a wipeable tray
Allergy check for oats; use paper if needed
activities.setup: Tray table with pets seated on a towel “placemat.” Limit 2–3 children.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a pet to feed.
2. Scoop food into a bowl.
3. Offer pretend water.
4. Wipe the pet’s mouth.
5. Say “all done” and rest the pet.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Is your pet hungry?
Scoop, scoop.
More or all done?
Wipe, wipe — clean face.
Thank you, helper.
activities.observationOpportunities: Observe scooping control, sequencing, pretend feeding language, and cleanup willingness.
activities.safetyNotes: No choking-size pieces. Supervise oats (mouthing). Paper kibble for under-2 mouthers if needed. Allergy awareness.
activities.cleanupTips: Sweep oats; recycle paper kibble; wash bowls.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Use paper kibble only for easier cleanup.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Do scooping at an outdoor sensory table.
teacherTips: Demonstrate one scoop at a time.
Keep water pretend-only unless doing a separate water-play day.

substitutions.use: Torn paper, pom-pom LARGE only for older toddlers, or dry pasta wheels if safe for age

activities.adaptations: Pre-fill bowls for children who need simpler roles. Offer larger scoops.
activities.extensions: Sort “dog food” vs “cat food” bowls by pet picture.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger children hand a pre-filled bowl; older scoop independently.
observationPrompts: Did scooping improve with practice?
Did the child narrate feeding?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler table with stuffed pets, bowls, and scoops of oats or paper kibble on a tray. Realistic daycare photo. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Pet Story Exploration
activities.objective: Share a short pet/vet picture book and invite toddlers to point, name, and connect story pets to classroom pets.
activities.description: Small-group read-aloud with lots of pointing and short questions. Toddlers may hold a stuffed pet while listening.
activities.materials:
Age-appropriate pet/vet book (e.g., Biscuit Visits the Doctor or Harry the Dirty Dog)
1–2 stuffed pets
Cushions
activities.preparation:
Preview book length; plan 2–3 stop-and-talk pages
Place pets by the reading spot
activities.setup: Cozy cushion circle for 3–4 toddlers.
activities.steps:
1. Show the cover and name the pet.
2. Read briefly, pausing to point.
3. Invite toddlers to show their stuffed pet when the story pet appears.
4. Ask one feeling or care question.
5. Retell with two picture walk pages.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Where is the dog?
What does the helper do?
Is the pet scared or brave?
Can your pet listen too?
What happened next?
activities.observationOpportunities: Attention span, pointing, vocabulary echoes, emotional responses to story events.
activities.safetyNotes: Board books preferred. Keep group small. No forcing lap sitting.
activities.cleanupTips: Return book to shelf; pets to basket.
teacherTips: Let toddlers “read” by turning pages after.

substitutions.use: Any short pet board book from your library

activities.adaptations: Offer standing listening. Provide a fidget pet to hold.
activities.extensions: Act out one page at the vet clinic center later.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants hear voice + look at large pictures; toddlers answer point questions.
observationPrompts: Did the child point to a named pet?
Did they stay for most of the short reading?

activities.title: Pet Care Discovery Table
activities.objective: Explore pet-care tools and textures through open-ended handling and matching tools to pets.
activities.description: Toddlers investigate brushes, cloths, bowls, and collars (large) on a discovery tray and try them with stuffed pets.
activities.materials:
Soft brushes
Washcloths
Bowls
Large ribbon collars
Stuffed pets
Tray
activities.preparation: Sanitize tools; remove small collar buckles if unsafe.
activities.setup: Low table tray with 3–4 tool types and 2 pets.
activities.steps:
1. Name each tool.
2. Invite children to try a brush on a pet.
3. Match bowl to pet.
4. Pack tools back on the tray.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What is this?
Brush, brush.
Which pet needs water?
Can you put it back?
activities.observationOpportunities: Tool use, matching, vocabulary, persistence.
activities.safetyNotes: Large tools only; supervise ribbons.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Floor tray works if table is busy.
teacherTips: Rotate only two tools at first.
activities.adaptations: Hand-over-hand brushing; fewer choices.
activities.extensions: Make a “dirty/clean” pet pretend contrast with a damp cloth.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers label tools for younger peers.
observationPrompts: Did the child try more than one tool?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Discovery tray with pet-care tools and stuffed pets on a daycare table. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Pet Bath Sensory Station
activities.objective: Wash washable pets in shallow soapy water to practice pouring, scrubbing, and caregiving sensory play.
activities.description: Toddlers bathe plastic/washable pets in a shallow tub using cloths and cups, then towel-dry them.
activities.materials:
Shallow sensory tub
Warm soapy water (mild)
Washable plastic pets
Washcloths
Cups
Towels
Smocks
activities.preparation:
Fill shallow water (low level)
Set drying towels beside tub
Allergy/skin sensitivity check
activities.setup: Sensory table or floor tub on a towel with 2–3 children max.
activities.steps:
1. Put on smocks.
2. Dip cloth and gently wash pet.
3. Pour a little rinse water.
4. Towel dry.
5. Rest clean pets on a towel “bed.”
activities.teacherLanguage:
Wash the paws.
Is the water wet?
Pour slowly.
Dry, dry.
So clean!
activities.observationOpportunities: Sensory tolerance, pouring control, caregiving talk, turn-taking at the tub.
activities.safetyNotes: Shallow water only; constant supervision; no standing water unattended; slip hazards; keep soap mild.
activities.cleanupTips: Dump water; sanitize tub; hang towels.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Use damp cloths only (no open water) on a tray for a “dry bath.”
teacherTips: Have a dry-only station for water-avoidant children.
activities.adaptations: Offer sealed water bag to press instead of open water. Short turns.
activities.extensions: Compare dirty vs clean cloths.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants: caregiver-led cloth wipe on a large toy; toddlers scoop/pour.
observationPrompts: Did the child tolerate wet textures?
Did pouring stay controlled with support?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Shallow daycare sensory tub with soapy water, plastic pets, cloths, and towels. Realistic photo. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Puppy Obstacle Course
activities.objective: Crawl, climb, and balance on a simple “puppy path” to build coordination and confidence.
activities.description: Toddlers move through a short obstacle path: tunnel crawl, cushion climb, and tape balance line while pretending to be puppies.
activities.materials:
Play tunnel or chair tunnel with blanket
Floor cushions
Painter’s tape line
Optional cones
activities.preparation: Build a short 3-station path; test stability.
activities.setup: Clear open path with start and finish stuffed-pet markers.
activities.steps:
1. Show the puppy path.
2. Crawl through the tunnel.
3. Climb over two cushions.
4. Walk the tape line.
5. Celebrate at the finish pet.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Crawl, puppy!
Over the pillows.
Balance on the line.
You did it!
Want to go again?
activities.observationOpportunities: Crawling strength, climbing safety awareness, balance, persistence.
activities.safetyNotes: Spot climbers; soft landings; no stacking unstable furniture; one-way traffic.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Use playground tunnel/equipment with same sequence.
teacherTips: Offer a bypass for children who dislike tunnels.
activities.adaptations: Wider tape line; hand support; skip crawl if needed.
activities.extensions: Carry a lightweight stuffed pet through the path.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers do one station; older complete all three.
observationPrompts: Which station needed the most support?

activities.title: Brush and Groom Station
activities.objective: Strengthen hand muscles and caregiving focus by brushing stuffed pets with soft brushes.
activities.description: Toddlers brush fur, “clean ears” with cloths, and comb with wide-tooth toddler combs on stuffed pets.
activities.materials:
Soft brushes
Wide combs
Washcloths
Stuffed pets
Mirror (optional)
activities.preparation: Sanitize brushes; set grooming caddy.
activities.setup: Small table with pets on towels.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a pet.
2. Brush from head toward tail.
3. Wipe face gently.
4. Look in mirror with pet (optional).
5. Put tools away.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Brush gently.
Long strokes.
Clean face.
Does your pet like brushing?
activities.observationOpportunities: Grasp, stroke direction, gentleness, tool cleanup.
activities.safetyNotes: Soft tools only; no sharp combs; supervise mirrors.
activities.cleanupTips: Return tools to caddy; lint-roll pets if needed.
activities.adaptations: Hand-over-hand; larger brush handles.
activities.extensions: Count “five brushes” together.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants feel a soft brush on their own hand with caregiver consent/cue.
observationPrompts: Did grip strengthen across the turn?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Grooming station with soft brushes and stuffed pets on towels. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Pet Owner Pretend Play
activities.objective: Role-play being a pet owner who cares for, walks, and rests a stuffed pet.
activities.description: Toddlers put on a simple helper badge, attach a large ribbon leash to a stuffed pet, walk a short indoor path, then settle the pet for a nap.
activities.materials:
Stuffed pets
Large ribbon leashes (short)
Paper helper badges
Blanket beds
Optional shopping bag for “pet store”
activities.preparation: Tie short leashes; make big badges; clear walk path.
activities.setup: Home corner with beds + short walking loop.
activities.steps:
1. Put on a helper badge.
2. Choose a pet and leash.
3. Walk slowly on the path.
4. Return for water/food pretend.
5. Nap time on blankets.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Hold the leash.
Walking feet.
Home time.
Night-night, pet.
activities.observationOpportunities: Role persistence, leash control, nurturing behaviors.
activities.safetyNotes: Short leashes only; no wrapping around necks; supervise ribbons.
activities.adaptations: Carry pet without leash; shorter path.
activities.extensions: Visit the vet clinic center with the pet.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers help younger clip badges.
observationPrompts: Did the child complete walk + rest sequence?

activities.title: Vet Examination Station
activities.objective: Practice a simple check-up sequence: look, listen, bandage, and comfort.
activities.description: Toddlers examine stuffed pets using a light-up or toy otoscope stand-in, stethoscope, and stickers as “health spots.”
activities.materials:
Exam table
Stuffed pets
Toy stethoscope
Flashlight (eyes down)
Large bandage fabric
Dot stickers
activities.preparation: Remove unsafe kit pieces; test flashlight.
activities.setup: One exam table for two children with a waiting pet.
activities.steps:
1. Place pet on the table.
2. Look at eyes/ears gently.
3. Listen to chest.
4. Add a bandage or sticker.
5. Comfort with a hug and rest.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Looking… looking.
I hear a heartbeat.
Bandage on.
All better?
Hug your pet.
activities.observationOpportunities: Sequencing, gentleness, symbolic tool use.
activities.safetyNotes: Flashlight never in eyes; no small stickers for heavy mouthers (use fabric bandage instead).
teacherTips: Keep sequence to 3 steps if needed.
activities.adaptations: One-step exam only; adult models first.
activities.extensions: Mark a paper chart with a big stamp.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Preschoolers can be scribes; toddlers do hands-on care.
observationPrompts: How many exam steps did they attempt?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Exam table with stuffed pet, stethoscope, and bandage strips in a real classroom. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Animal Rescue Sensory Bin
activities.objective: Rescue buried plastic pets from a safe sensory filler using hands and scoops, building persistence and fine-motor strength.
activities.description: Toddlers dig in shredded paper or kinetic sand to find hidden pets and place them in a “rescue basket.”
activities.materials:
Sensory bin
Shredded paper OR kinetic sand
Plastic pets
Scoops
Rescue basket
activities.preparation: Hide 4–6 pets; set rescue basket.
activities.setup: Bin on a towel with scoop caddy.
activities.steps:
1. Dig to find a pet.
2. Name the pet.
3. Place in rescue basket.
4. Cover and hide again for another turn.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Where is the cat?
Dig, dig.
You found it!
To the basket.
Who is missing?
activities.observationOpportunities: Persistence, scooping, labeling, sharing space.
activities.safetyNotes: Choose filler safe for mouthers; kinetic sand supervised; no small gravel.
activities.cleanupTips: Shake pets; return filler to sealed bin.
teacherTips: Hide only a few at a time.

substitutions.use: Shredded paper or water beads ONLY if age policy allows; prefer paper for toddlers

activities.adaptations: Partially visible pets for easier success.
activities.extensions: Rescue by color of pet.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants watch finds; toddlers dig.
observationPrompts: Did the child persist after a miss?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Sensory bin with shredded paper, plastic pets partially visible, rescue basket beside it. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Carry the Pet Challenge
activities.objective: Carry a stuffed pet carefully from one basket to another to practice balance, spatial awareness, and gentle transport.
activities.description: Toddlers walk a short path carrying a pet with two hands, stepping over a soft pool noodle, then place the pet in a bed basket.
activities.materials:
Stuffed pets
Start basket
Bed basket
Pool noodle or tape line
activities.preparation: Clear path; demonstrate two-hand carry.
activities.setup: Start basket → path → bed basket.
activities.steps:
1. Pick up pet with two hands.
2. Walk slowly.
3. Step over the noodle.
4. Place pet in bed.
5. Return for another if desired.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Two hands.
Slow walking feet.
Over.
Pet is safe in bed.
activities.observationOpportunities: Carry control, pace, following path.
activities.safetyNotes: No running; light pets only; spot step-over.
teacherTips: Cheer careful carries more than speed.
activities.adaptations: Shorter distance; adult spotter.
activities.extensions: Carry pet + a blanket.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers carry short distance only.
observationPrompts: Did they keep two-hand carry?

activities.title: Pet Health Chart Art
activities.objective: Create process art paw prints to celebrate pet care, focusing on stamping and color exploration rather than a perfect product.
activities.description: Toddlers stamp toy-animal paws or sponge “paws” into washable paint and onto paper charts labeled with their pet’s name by the teacher.
activities.materials:
Paper
Washable paint (2 colors)
Shallow trays
Plastic animal paws or sponges cut as paws
Smocks
Wipes
activities.preparation:
Write child’s name + “My Pet” on paper
Pour thin paint layers
Tape paper to table
activities.setup: Art table with two stamp choices and a drying rack.
activities.steps:
1. Put on a smock.
2. Dip paw stamp in paint.
3. Press onto paper.
4. Repeat with a second color if wanted.
5. Set chart to dry.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Dip.
Press.
What color is that paw?
Another one?
Your pet chart is drying.
activities.observationOpportunities: Stamp pressure, color choice, engagement length, name recognition when teacher writes.
activities.safetyNotes: Non-toxic paint; smocks; wipe hands; no tasting.

substitutions.use: Child’s fist as a “paw” with adult help

activities.adaptations: Hand-over-hand stamping; larger paper.
activities.extensions: Add sticker hearts after dry (large stickers).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants: caregiver-assisted footprint keepsake if family permits; toddlers stamp.
observationPrompts: Did the child try more than one stamp?
activities.imageBriefExample: Finished toddler paw-print chart on paper: uneven stamped paw prints in 1–2 washable paint colors, child’s name written by teacher, slight smudges, photographed on a classroom table. Looks child-made, not perfect. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Animal Investigation Center
activities.objective: Look closely at large pet photos and simple body-part cards to notice eyes, ears, tails, and fur.
activities.description: Toddlers use magnifying glasses (plastic) to examine large pet photos and match a soft pet to a picture.
activities.materials:
Large pet photos
Plastic magnifiers
Stuffed pets
Simple body-part cards (ear, tail, paw)
activities.preparation: Print/laminate large photos; remove tiny cards.
activities.setup: Science table with 3 photos and matching pets.
activities.steps:
1. Look at a photo with a magnifier.
2. Find eyes/ears/tail.
3. Match a stuffed pet to the photo.
4. Trace a tail with a finger.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What do you see?
Where are the ears?
Same or different?
Soft fur.
activities.observationOpportunities: Attention to detail, matching, vocabulary for body parts.
activities.safetyNotes: Large photos; magnifiers supervised; no glass.
activities.cleanupTips: Stack cards in a photo box.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Observe a classroom fish/pet if present, or outdoor birds from a window.

substitutions.use: Empty picture frame as a “look window”

activities.adaptations: Fewer photos; point-only responses.
activities.extensions: Sort pets into “fur” vs “feathers” with two baskets.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Preschoolers can count legs; toddlers match wholes.
observationPrompts: Did matching happen with support or independently?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Science table with large pet photos, plastic magnifier, and stuffed pets. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Build a Pet Home
activities.objective: Build a simple bed, box house, or block enclosure that can hold a stuffed pet.
activities.description: Toddlers use blocks, boxes, and blankets to create a home and test whether their pet fits inside.
activities.materials:
Blocks
Shoeboxes
Blankets/towels
Stuffed pets
Tape (teacher use)
activities.preparation: Collect boxes; open block area.
activities.setup: Floor building space with pets nearby.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a pet.
2. Build walls or place a blanket bed.
3. Try fitting the pet.
4. Adjust if needed.
5. “Good night” routine.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Does it fit?
Make it bigger.
Wall or bed?
Your pet has a home.
activities.observationOpportunities: Problem solving, spatial awareness, persistence after failed fit.
activities.safetyNotes: Stable structures only; no heavy blocks overhead; supervise boxes.
activities.cleanupTips: Blocks to shelf; flatten boxes if storing.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Build with outdoor blocks under shade.
activities.adaptations: Pre-build a three-block bed to personalize.
activities.extensions: Add a paper door sign with pet photo.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers add roofs; younger make blanket nests.
observationPrompts: Did they revise after a pet did not fit?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Block/box pet homes with stuffed pets tucked in, on a classroom rug. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Rescue Mission Adventure
activities.objective: Complete a pretend rescue path to bring pets to safety, combining movement and caregiving.
activities.description: Toddlers follow a path of mats to collect pets from “trees” (chairs) and deliver them to the clinic basket.
activities.materials:
Floor mats
Chairs as trees
Stuffed pets
Clinic basket
Optional siren sound (soft)
activities.preparation: Place pets on chairs; map path.
activities.setup: One-way rescue path ending at clinic.
activities.steps:
1. Hear the soft helper call.
2. Walk the mats.
3. Gently take a pet from a chair.
4. Deliver to clinic basket.
5. Cheer the rescue.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Helper coming!
Careful carry.
To the clinic.
Pet is safe.
activities.observationOpportunities: Path following, gentle retrieval, teamwork.
activities.safetyNotes: Pets at safe heights; no climbing chairs; walking feet.
activities.adaptations: Shorter path; adult carries with child.
activities.extensions: Two-pet rescue for older toddlers.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants receive a rescued pet for cuddle time.
observationPrompts: Was retrieval gentle?

activities.title: Walk the Pet Movement Game
activities.objective: Move start/stop with music while “walking” a pet to practice listening and body control.
activities.description: Toddlers hold a pet or leash and walk when music plays, freezing when it stops.
activities.materials:
Music player
Stuffed pets or short leashes
Open space
activities.preparation: Choose calm walking song; clear space.
activities.setup: Circle or line with pets ready.
activities.steps:
1. Hold your pet.
2. Music on — walking feet.
3. Music off — freeze hug.
4. Repeat 4–5 rounds.
5. Sit and rest pets.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Walking…
Freeze!
Hug your pet.
Ready again?
activities.observationOpportunities: Auditory listening, impulse control, coordinated walking.
activities.safetyNotes: No running; space children; short leashes.
teacherTips: Offer seated rocking for children who need less locomotion.
activities.adaptations: Visual stop/go cards; seated version.
activities.extensions: Add tip-toe vs stomp pet walks.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants sway with caregiver; toddlers walk/freeze.
observationPrompts: Did freeze happen with fewer prompts over time?

activities.title: Collar Decorating
activities.objective: Decorate a large paper collar strip with stickers and stamps as an open-ended fine-motor art experience.
activities.description: Toddlers press stickers and stamps onto a wide paper collar, then tape it loosely around a stuffed pet (teacher assists sizing).
activities.materials:
Wide paper strips
Large stickers
Stampers + washable ink
Tape
Stuffed pets
Smocks
activities.preparation: Pre-cut large strips; sort big stickers only.
activities.setup: Art table with strips taped down lightly.
activities.steps:
1. Decorate the strip.
2. Choose stickers/stamps freely.
3. Teacher helps fit collar on pet.
4. Show pet to friends.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Where will this sticker go?
Stamp!
Your pet looks fancy.
All done?
activities.observationOpportunities: Pincer grasp, planning sticker placement, pride in sharing.
activities.safetyNotes: Large stickers only; monitor mouthing; ink non-toxic.
activities.adaptations: Pre-sticky strip; larger stickers.
activities.extensions: Add a paper name tag dictated by child.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers place 2–3 stickers; older fill the strip.
observationPrompts: Did fine-motor grasp look secure?
activities.imageBriefExample: Finished toddler-decorated paper pet collar on a stuffed dog: uneven stickers, simple stamps, slightly crooked tape, real classroom table. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Pet Adoption Center
activities.objective: Pretend to choose, name, and “adopt” a classroom pet for the day, practicing decision-making and gentle care.
activities.description: Toddlers visit an adoption shelf of pets, choose one, dictate a name for a teacher tag, and promise gentle care.
activities.materials:
Shelf of stuffed pets
Paper name tags
Marker
Adoption basket
Picture signs
activities.preparation: Set shelf; prepare blank tags.
activities.setup: Adoption center next to clinic with a waiting line of tape marks.
activities.steps:
1. Look at available pets.
2. Choose one.
3. Tell a name (or sound).
4. Teacher writes tag.
5. Take pet to a home bed.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Which pet will you choose?
What is the name?
Gentle care.
Welcome home.
activities.observationOpportunities: Choice-making, language for names, caregiving follow-through.
activities.safetyNotes: Supervise tags (no pin backs); large pets.
activities.cleanupTips: Return unadopted pets; save tags if reusing.
teacherTips: Accept any name including animal sounds.
Limit to one pet per child if needed.
activities.adaptations: Offer two choices only; point to choose.
activities.extensions: Visit vet clinic for a first check-up after adoption.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers help younger pick.
observationPrompts: Did the child follow through with care after choosing?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Classroom adoption shelf with stuffed pets, name tags, and a welcome sign. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Pet Parade
activities.objective: Celebrate the week with a joyful pet parade that reviews gentle walking and pet words.
activities.description: Toddlers parade with their adopted or favorite pets to a simple rhythm instrument beat, then bow and rest.
activities.materials:
Stuffed pets
Drum or shaker
Path markers
Optional helper badges
activities.preparation: Clear parade path; choose a steady beat.
activities.setup: Line up at start cone; audience cushions for peers waiting turns.
activities.steps:
1. Line up with pets.
2. March to the beat.
3. Wave to friends.
4. Bow at the finish.
5. Rest pets in a circle.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Pets ready?
March, march.
Wave!
Take a bow.
Rest time.
activities.observationOpportunities: Group participation, rhythm matching, pride/sharing.
activities.safetyNotes: Walking feet; spaced line; no running with leashes.
activities.adaptations: Seated parade with pet waves; shorter route.
activities.extensions: Each child names their pet for the group.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants watch and bounce; toddlers march.
observationPrompts: Did the child stay with the group beat?

activities.title: Create a Favorite Pet Craft
activities.objective: Make an open-ended collage or paint portrait of a favorite pet using large paper and simple collage pieces.
activities.description: Toddlers glue large paper shapes and yarn bits onto a pet outline or free collage, focusing on process.
activities.materials:
Large paper
Pre-cut large shapes (ears, circles)
Glue sticks
Yarn pieces (short)
Crayons
Smocks
activities.preparation: Pre-cut shapes; portion glue; optional light pet outline.
activities.setup: Art table with shared shape trays.
activities.steps:
1. Choose paper.
2. Glue shapes anywhere.
3. Add crayon marks.
4. Add yarn if wanted.
5. Dry flat.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Where should the ear go?
Sticky glue.
Tell me about your pet.
You worked hard.
activities.observationOpportunities: Glue control, creative choices, language about the pet.
activities.safetyNotes: Short yarn only; glue sticks preferred; supervise.
activities.adaptations: Contact paper sticky collage for easier success.
activities.extensions: Dictate a sentence about the pet for the back of the paper.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger toddlers stick 2–3 shapes; older add details.
observationPrompts: Did the child describe their pet?
activities.imageBriefExample: Finished toddler pet collage: uneven glued ears/shapes, crayon scribbles, short yarn, imperfect placement on classroom paper. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Pet Sensory Exploration
activities.objective: Compare soft, smooth, and bumpy pet-related textures using large safe samples.
activities.description: Toddlers feel fabric fur squares, smooth bowls, and bumpy rubber pet toys, sorting into soft/not soft baskets if interested.
activities.materials:
Fur fabric squares
Smooth plastic bowls
Bumpy rubber pet toys
Two baskets (soft / not soft)
activities.preparation: Sanitize textures; avoid shedding fur that mouths easily.
activities.setup: Sensory tray with two sort baskets.
activities.steps:
1. Feel a texture.
2. Name soft/smooth/bumpy.
3. Optional sort into baskets.
4. Revisit favorites.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Soft?
Bumpy!
Where does it go?
You like that one.
activities.observationOpportunities: Sensory preferences, sorting interest, descriptive language.
activities.safetyNotes: Large pieces; watch mouthing of fabric; sanitize.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Add natural smooth stones only if too large to choke and supervised.
activities.adaptations: One texture at a time for sensitive children.
activities.extensions: Blindfold feel game for older toddlers (optional).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants: caregiver-guided one soft square.
observationPrompts: Which textures were preferred or avoided?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Texture tray with fur squares, bowls, bumpy toys, and two sort baskets. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Build a Pet Playground
activities.objective: Design a playful playground for stuffed pets using blocks, ramps, and tunnels.
activities.description: Toddlers build slides/ramps and tunnels then test whether a pet can go through or slide down.
activities.materials:
Blocks
Cardboard ramps
Tunnels
Stuffed/plastic pets
activities.preparation: Stage ramp pieces; clear build zone.
activities.setup: Block center with pets waiting on a tray.
activities.steps:
1. Build a ramp or tunnel.
2. Send a pet through/down.
3. Fix if it falls.
4. Add a second feature.
5. Tour the playground.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Will it slide?
Try again.
Up or down?
Your playground is ready.
activities.observationOpportunities: Cause/effect testing, collaboration, redesign after failure.
activities.safetyNotes: Stable builds; no high towers near walking paths.
activities.adaptations: Provide a starter ramp.
activities.extensions: Race two pets down ramps.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older build; younger test pets.
observationPrompts: Did they redesign after a tumble?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Block pet playground with ramp and tunnel and stuffed pets. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Junior Veterinarian Graduation
activities.objective: Close the week with a simple Pet Helper Celebration that reviews gentle care words—not a formal academic graduation.
activities.description: Toddlers wear helper badges, show a favorite pet, share one care word or action, and receive a sticker high-five.
activities.materials:
Helper badges
Stuffed pets
Large celebration sign “Pet Helpers”
Stickers
Song
activities.preparation: Make badges; post celebration sign; choose a short song.
activities.setup: Circle cushions with pets on laps.
activities.steps:
1. Sing a short pet song.
2. Each child shows a pet (optional).
3. Teacher names one gentle thing they did this week.
4. Sticker high-five.
5. Group cheer: “Gentle helpers!”
activities.teacherLanguage:
You were a gentle helper.
What did your pet need?
High five!
We care for pets.
activities.observationOpportunities: Pride, recall of care routines, willingness to share in a group.
activities.safetyNotes: Keep celebration short; no pressure to speak; large stickers.
teacherTips: Rename away from “graduation” pressure if families prefer.
activities.adaptations: Allow nonverbal show-and-share; adult speaks for child if invited.
activities.extensions: Family note: “Ask what pet we cared for today.”
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants get a soft song + cuddle pet; toddlers share.
observationPrompts: Did the child show recognition of a care routine?
activities.decisionNote: Reframed as Pet Helper Celebration; avoid academic graduation tone
